newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Pro-Israeli militiaman wounded in Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Pro-Israeli militiaman wounded in Lebanon.

text.p: A member of the pro-Israel South Lebanon Army militia was seriously wounded on Sunday by a guerrilla missile fired at his outpost in Israel's South Lebanon occupation zone, Israeli security sources said.
The sources said the incident occurred in the western sector of the 15-km-(nine-mile)-wide zone Israel carved out in 1985 to protect its northern border from Arab guerrilla attack.

On Saturday, the pro-Iranian Hizbollah group said its fighters fired Katyusha rockets into an Israeli outpost in south Lebanon, hours after an Israeli shell wounded a Lebanese woman north of the area.
Lebanon planned to complain about the attack to a five-nation committee monitoring an April 1996 ceasefire understanding which ended a 17-day Israeli blitz on Lebanon.

Under the terms of the ceasefire deal, Israeli forces and Lebanese guerrillas are banned from hitting civilian targets on both sides of the border. The deal does not ban Hizbollah from fighting Israeli troops and their local militia allies.
